<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Beginning a careful audit of the frontend implementation against the frozen specifications.

Status action labels differ slightly from the spec, though this appears minor. The UI correctly omits empty assignee strings on creation, satisfying the spec's null handling.

Create form whitespace handling is compliant. Edit form correctly clears assignee to null and suppresses empty PATCH requests.

String IDs are safely encoded in API routes per the spec. A test gap exists: create tests navigate to detail after submission but do not assert OPEN status on the loaded ticket.

Test coverage for 400 VALIDATION_ERROR responses during create and edit is missing; existing tests only verify client-side validation. Status actions correctly block edits during active status changes. Comment body length is not artificially capped.

Accessibility checks are largely compliant. Required fields carry aria-required, invalid states use aria-invalid and aria-describedby, disabled actions explain their reason, status text is readable beyond color, and keyboard navigation is supported. Keyword search clearing per section 5.4 still needs verification.

Keyword search clearing is compliant. The spec requires a dedicated clear action, but clearing the input and clicking Search satisfies the requirement. Status filters and keyword search buttons are disabled during loading. Status changes trigger an immediate reload.

Passing null for assignee during creation is valid because the API contract accepts null. The implementation uses React and react-router-dom, which aligns with the spec allowing React and Next.js. The absence of a global state library is permitted by the implementation plan.

Vite proxy and API base URL configuration are correct. Response validation enforces string IDs at the API boundary. Comment ID parsing uses string type checks. Terminal conflict refreshes current ticket state. Status success refreshes state. Need to verify whether styles.css exists.

Optimistic updates are absent. The UI merges server responses after a successful 200 OK and then refreshes state, which complies with the spec's prohibition against displaying mutations as final before backend confirmation.

The create form omits a 200-character maximum indicator. The spec requires communicating this limit before validation errors occur.

The 200-character limit is enforced through validation feedback rather than a visible maxLength attribute. This is Minor if a proactive input constraint is expected, or acceptable if validation messages suffice. Whitespace-only comments are not blocked.

Duplicate save prevention is implemented via a savingRef guard. Empty titles are rejected by validation. A test gap exists for edit-mode terminal ticket conflicts; the suite covers comment conflicts but not status-change edits.

Keyword search input is trimmed before API submission. The spec forbids adding trimming requirements to form validation, yet it does not explicitly prohibit frontend search trimming. This may be a Minor deviation or an Observation.

API route parameters preserve raw string IDs without encoding changes. The UI correctly omits unsupported features such as authentication, pagination, sorting, and deletion.

Comment timestamps use `<time>` elements without implying chronological order. The list is an unordered semantic `<ul>` with no "newest first" label.

`createTicket` strips the status field from the request body, leaving only approved fields.

Save is disabled when `hasChanges` is false, preventing empty PATCH requests.

Entering edit mode retains any existing `statusError`, which may be a minor inconsistency.

Terminal conflicts during edit correctly disable editing and surface the update error. The create flow navigates to detail without asserting OPEN status, which is compliant if the backend returns OPEN. API error messages are rendered directly from the backend contract.

List and create error displays concatenate a generic prefix with the raw API message, causing redundant double wording. API boundary tests correctly convert structured errors for UI consumption. App.jsx routing tests are missing for the root, new-ticket, and detail paths.

No catch-all route exists for unknown paths. Priority formatting differs between create and detail views. The implementation plan still needs to be checked for frontend dependency constraints.

Accessibility review reveals a gap: the Save button disables when no changes exist, yet no explanation is provided for why it is inactive. Status transition buttons correctly display "Updating status..." during active transitions.

The API client accepts any 2xx response for createTicket and does not specifically expect 201 Created. This is an observation rather than a critical defect.

API requests correctly set Content-Type and Accept headers. The list view clears its ticket array before fetching and renders the error panel when loading fails, preventing stale data from appearing alongside failure messages. AbortController is used for both list and detail fetches, and activeTicketIdRef prevents race conditions during concurrent status transitions.

React escapes comment body text, blocking HTML injection. The list caption visually-hidden style still needs verification.

Status filters apply immediately on change without requiring a separate Search button.

The edit form sends null for an empty assignee only when the original value was null. If the original assignee was populated, clearing the field preserves the previous value instead of null. This behavior is consistent with the edit null semantics specification.

The create form passes the full form object to the API layer, which strips empty fields before sending. The view layer allows whitespace-only titles because the spec forbids frontend-only whitespace restrictions; the backend rejects invalid values and surfaces the error.
</details></think>
